overview: The committee reviewed reports on summer learning recovery and finalized labor agreements regarding staff COVID-19 testing and vaccination protocols for the 2021-2022 school year. Members also addressed operational challenges, including a regional bus driver shortage and classroom accessibility for left-handed students.

items.title: Consent Agenda and Minutes
items.summary: Approved the June 14 meeting minutes as amended to clarify the identity of a public speaker.

items.title: Summer Programming and School Opening Report
items.summary: District staff reported on special education services, math and literacy acceleration camps, and social-emotional programs designed to transition students back to in-person learning. Enrollment data for the new school year showed an increase in kindergarten sections and specialized programming needs.

items.title: Public Health Update
items.summary: Health officials detailed the district's COVID-19 surveillance and symptomatic testing programs and confirmed that the mask mandate would remain in place through October. Discussions also addressed the academic support of quarantined students and vaccination rates within the school population.

items.title: Shore Educational Collaborative Capital Plan
items.summary: Approved a 10-year capital improvement plan for the collaborative after confirming that any potential future asset dissolution would be handled proportionally among member districts.

items.title: Labor Relations and Testing Agreements
items.summary: Endorsed tentative agreements with bargaining units requiring weekly COVID-19 testing and reporting of vaccination status for staff.

items.title: Operations and Transportation Update
items.summary: The administration reported on a pilot program providing free MBTA passes to high schoolers and ongoing challenges with the regional bus driver shortage. Officials committed to using routing software to improve efficiency and better coordinate transportation for out-of-district students.

items.title: MASC Delegate Selection
items.summary: Appointed Paul Ruseau as the voting delegate and Jenny Graham as the alternate for the annual MASC/MASS conference.

items.title: Classroom Accessibility and Left-Handed Desks
items.summary: Approved a resolution requiring that 10% of desks in high school classrooms be configured for left-handed students by January 2022 to remove learning barriers. The district will investigate universal desk options to replace aging infrastructure at the high school.
